## 2

I understand why some images might seem questionable, especially when most of us rely on organizations and technology we haven’t personally tested. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on one space agency or a single photograph. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is round, and time zones and satellite communication all fit a globe far better than a flat model. Independent countries, companies, universities, and amateur observers have also tracked satellites and photographed Earth. It’s reasonable to ask questions, but the overall evidence strongly supports a spherical Earth.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

Violet light is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, so much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us. The remaining reds and oranges make the sunset colorful.

雨下了一整夜，细密的雨丝在昏黄的路灯下交织，像一层看不见尽头的帘子。屋檐不断滴水，落在青石路上，发出清脆而规律的声响。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，车轮卷起水花，灯光在积水里晃成模糊的金色。窗玻璃蒙着雾气，街上的行人撑着伞匆匆走过，脚步声很快又被雨声吞没。夜色湿润而安静，仿佛整座城市都在这场雨中慢慢沉睡。
